intro_html: Lean chicken breast simmered in a coconut red curry with a sweet-salty backbone of fish sauce and brown sugar, all over rice. Each bowl brings 45 grams of protein for about $2.29. Lean has never tasted less like a punishment.
cost_closing_html: About $2.29 a bowl for coconut red curry chicken over rice. The restaurant version is $15 a plate, which means this batch pays for itself before you finish the second container.
shop_smart: Boneless skinless chicken breast is the whole protein bill at about $12.86 for 5.25 pounds. Club-pack pricing under $2.50 a pound is the target, and this recipe is why you keep some in the freezer.
Red curry paste and fish sauce are the two flavor bottles, and both keep for months. Their true cost per batch is a couple of dollars against jars that season many dinners.

Coconut milk is the only other line that matters at 3.5 cans. Brown sugar, oil, and rice are pantry riders, so the register total is mostly chicken and coconut, which is exactly how a curry should look.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Cut the chicken breast into bite-size pieces and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high and brown the chicken in batches until cooked to 165F, then remove.
In the same pot, cook the green onions, garlic, and jalapeno for 2 minutes, then add the red curry paste and fry it 1 to 2 minutes until it darkens and smells intense.
Pour in the coconut milk, stir in the fish sauce and brown sugar, and simmer about 5 minutes until the curry is smooth and lightly thickened.
Return the chicken, simmer another minute or two to coat, then finish with the lime juice and cilantro.
Serve the coconut curry chicken over the rice.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot with rice and chicken, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Portion to that number and each bowl lands at about 637 calories with 45 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $2.29 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

steps: Cook the rice and set aside.
Brown seasoned chicken breast pieces in oil to 165F, then remove.
Cook green onions, garlic, and jalapeno, then fry the red curry paste.
Pour in the coconut milk with fish sauce and brown sugar and simmer into a curry.
Return the chicken, finish with lime and cilantro, serve over rice, and portion into 14 containers.
